messages:
alex: Heads up — I ran the node sample app with the new auth-retry middleware and noticed logs flip to DEBUG for retried requests and the request-id value changes mid-flight. Repro steps below.

sam: Ugh. I saw something similar in go SDK last week but thought it was different.

alex: Repro:
1) start sampleapp: `yarn start:sample-node`
2) hit /generate with large prompt and X-Retry-After forcing 502 from stubbed backend
3) observe logs: first attempt INFO with request-id abc123, retry attempt DEBUG and request-id abc124.

maria: Can you paste the logger config? Might be a log-level env toggle leaking.

alex: Logger is tiny:
```
const logger = createLogger({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info' });
app.use((req,res,next) => { req.requestId = uuid(); next(); });
app.use(authRetryMiddleware()); // from SDK
app.use(otelHook());
```

olivia: Looks like order: you assign requestId, then authRetryMiddleware likely re-issues new req object/context and otelHook attaches after. If retry recreates request, requestId may be regenerated.

sam: In Go we had retry wrap replace context.Context causing traceid to be dropped. Fix was to pass through existing context when reissuing request.

alex: Quick fix I tried: move otelHook and reqId assignment inside authRetryMiddleware before outgoing call. That preserved requestId but made logs noisy for non-retried paths.

maria: Is the SDK currently mutating `req` or returning a fresh object? It's supposed to clone headers only, not mutate context/state.

alex: From debugging, SDK's retry path calls `await handler({...request, headers: newHeaders})` which creates a new object. Our middleware uses `req.requestId` not headers. So it's lost.

olivia: Two options:
- Have SDK carry `x-request-id` header through retries (preferred)
- Or make otel hooks attach request-id to headers before retries and read back after.

sam: I can PR to node SDK to preserve headers + traceparent across retries. Also add a small note in sampleapp that middleware order matters.

alex: Created https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/412 - preserves trace headers and copies request-id if present. cc @maria @olivia

ci-bot: CI passed for unit tests, integration flaky on windows (known).

maria: Nice. For short term, add a one-liner in docs: 'If you use authRetryMiddleware, ensure request-id/otel hooks run before or configure SDK to preserve headers.' Maybe a troubleshooting snippet.

alex: Thanks — marking workaround in sampleapp README and will flip in SDK PR once green. :thumbsup:

olivia: Also add a small regression test: simulate retry and assert same x-request-id header across attempts.

sam: I'll add go SDK ticket to mirror fix.
